The invention relates to a reciprocating piston engine comprising a crankshaft and at least one piston connected to the crankshaft by means of a length-adjustable connecting rod. By changing the effective length of the connecting rod, the compression ratio of the engine can be varied during operation or between different operating states.

The connecting rod comprises two rod parts that are telescopically displaceable relative to one another. These rod parts can be moved between different length positions in order to increase or decrease the overall length of the connecting rod. The relative displacement of the rod parts is controlled by a length adjustment device, which is preferably supplied with hydraulic pressure, in particular oil pressure, for setting and/or locking the desired connecting rod length.

For this purpose, the length adjustment device can be selectively connected to, or separated from, an oil pressure line. This connection is controlled by an electrically switchable control valve. Depending on the switching state of the control valve, pressurized oil is supplied to the length adjustment device or discharged or blocked, thereby enabling adjustment or retention of the connecting rod length.

The control valve is actuated inductively. To this end, an induction device is fixed to the connecting rod and is electrically connected to the control valve. The induction device is configured to generate an electrical current when exposed to a changing magnetic field. This induced current is then used to switch or operate the control valve without requiring a permanent wired electrical connection to the moving connecting rod.

A magnet device is arranged in a stationary or rotating engine component, in particular fixed to the crank housing or to the crankshaft. During operation of the engine, relative movement between the magnet device and the induction device produces the magnetic field variation required to induce current in the induction device. This current enables electrical actuation of the control valve on the connecting rod.

As a result, the length adjustment device can be controlled in a flexible and reliable manner while avoiding complex electrical wiring to the reciprocating or rotating connecting rod. The arrangement is simple, compact, and space-saving, and it permits robust adjustment of the engine compression ratio by changing the effective length of the connecting rod. This enables efficient adaptation of the engine to different load and operating conditions.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a reciprocating piston engine, in particular an internal combustion engine, having at least one cylinder, a piston movable in the cylinder, a crankshaft, and a connecting rod which connects the piston to the crankshaft. The connecting rod is designed to be telescopically length-adjustable so that the effective distance between the piston pin and the crank pin can be varied during operation. By changing this effective connecting-rod length, the top dead center position of the piston is altered, thereby enabling adjustment of the compression ratio of the engine.

For this purpose, the connecting rod comprises an oil-fed adjustment device. The adjustment device may include hydraulic chambers, pistons, locking elements, control passages, or similar components by means of which the connecting rod can be extended, shortened, or held in a selected length position. The supply and discharge of oil to the adjustment device are controlled by an electrically switchable valve arranged on or in the connecting rod. This valve is inductively actuated and can be switched between different positions in order to control the hydraulic pressure conditions in the adjustment device. In this way, the length of the connecting rod can be changed in a targeted manner, allowing the engine to operate with different compression ratios depending on load, speed, efficiency requirements, or emissions requirements.

A key feature of the engine is the manner in which electrical energy is supplied to the valve. Instead of using complex wiring, slip rings, or other mechanically sensitive electrical connections to the moving connecting rod, the connecting rod carries an induction device. This induction device is arranged so that, during rotation of the crankshaft and movement of the connecting rod, it passes through or near a magnetic field generated by a magnet fixed relative to the engine structure. The magnet may be mounted on the crankcase, on another stationary engine component, or on the crankshaft. As a result of the relative movement between the magnet and the induction device, an electric current is induced in the connecting-rod-mounted induction device.

The induced current is used to energize the electrically switchable valve. When the valve is energized, it changes its switching state and thereby influences the oil flow in the adjustment device. This makes it possible to control the hydraulic mechanism of the telescopic connecting rod without requiring a permanent wired electrical connection to the connecting rod. The arrangement is compact because the energy-generating components can be placed in the immediate vicinity of the connecting rod and crankshaft. It is also robust because it avoids exposed cables or contact-based current transfer devices in the highly dynamic crankcase environment.

The proposed system therefore provides a flexible and reliable mechanism for varying the compression ratio of a reciprocating piston engine. By enabling the connecting rod length to be adjusted hydraulically and the control valve to be supplied with current inductively, the design combines efficient compression-ratio control with a simple and durable energy transmission concept. This can improve engine efficiency, reduce fuel consumption, optimize performance over a wide operating range, and contribute to lower emissions.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps point to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

Although “the” may seem simple, it gives sentences clarity and direction. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. We use it in everyday phrases such as “the sun,” “the world,” “the future,” and “the truth.” Without it, English would sound less natural and often less precise.

The word “the” also appears in titles, names, and important expressions. It can make something feel unique or significant, as in “the best choice” or “the final answer.” Because of this, “the” is more than just a small word—it is a key part of how English creates meaning.

In short, “the” proves that even the simplest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention involving a reciprocating piston engine with a telescopically length-adjustable connecting rod and an inductively powered electrically switchable oil control valve.
counterfactuals.output: A reciprocating piston engine includes a crankshaft, a piston movable in a cylinder, and a connecting rod coupling the piston to the crankshaft, the connecting rod having a telescopically length-adjustable arrangement for varying an effective connecting rod length and thereby adjusting a compression ratio of the engine. A hydraulic adjustment chamber associated with the connecting rod is supplied with engine oil through an oil circuit, and an electrically switchable oil control valve selectively controls oil flow to and/or from the adjustment chamber to lock, extend, retract, or permit adjustment of the telescopic connecting rod. The oil control valve is mounted on or within the connecting rod and is supplied with electrical power inductively from a stationary or engine-mounted primary coil to a secondary coil carried by the moving connecting rod, thereby avoiding wired electrical connections to the reciprocating and rotating assembly. Control electronics actuate the valve in response to engine operating parameters to selectively change the effective length of the connecting rod during engine operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent abstract for a space-saving variable compression ratio mechanism in which a two-part telescopic connecting rod is connected to oil pressure lines through a control valve powered by an induction device fixed to the rod.
counterfactuals.output: A variable compression ratio mechanism for an internal combustion engine includes a telescopic connecting rod having a first rod part and a second rod part movable relative to one another to vary an effective length of the connecting rod and thereby change a compression ratio of an associated cylinder. The telescopic connecting rod is hydraulically actuated by oil pressure supplied through at least one oil pressure line in communication with an internal chamber of the connecting rod. A control valve mounted on or integrated with the connecting rod selectively connects the oil pressure line to the chamber to extend, retract, or lock the telescopic rod parts. The control valve is electrically powered by an induction device fixed to the connecting rod, the induction device generating electrical energy from relative motion and/or a magnetic field during engine operation. By locating the induction-powered control valve on the connecting rod and using existing oil pressure passages for actuation, the mechanism provides compact, space-saving control of connecting rod length without requiring external wiring to the moving rod assembly.
